profile.campus: Red Oak Campus, Compass Datacenters Dallas-Fort Worth market
profile.address: Ellis County, TX (Red Oak development campus, easternmost row, south)
profile.reading: This OpenStreetMap record is one of eleven adjacent building footprints in Compass Datacenters Red Oak development, a wholesale data center campus in Ellis County, Texas, just south of the Dallas-Fort Worth core. This particular footprint sits in the easternmost row of the campus, the southern of two buildings arranged along that row. Compass Datacenters own market materials describe this campus, part of its Dallas-Fort Worth market, as a 360 megawatt development that was still nearing completion as of the most recent site content reviewed, with a confirmed 200 million dollar expansion phase announced in April 2024 that added two buildings totaling more than 500,000 square feet, plausibly this easternmost pair of buildings given how recently they appear to have been added to the campus footprint, though that specific match could not be confirmed. A separate July 2026 company news item states that Red Oak now hosts seven data centers total, though that figure appears to describe the city of Red Oak as a whole rather than Compass own building count specifically, so it should not be read as confirming exactly how many of the eleven OpenStreetMap footprints in this cluster are Compass-operated versus operated by other companies also active in the area. Compass Datacenters was founded in 2011 by Chris Crosby, a former Digital Realty senior executive who remains the company CEO, and completed its first data center, a 1.2 megawatt facility, in 2012. The company is headquartered in Dallas, Texas, and describes its current ownership, per its own about-us page, as Ontario Teachers Pension Plan, RedBird Capital Partners, and company management. Beyond Dallas-Fort Worth, Compass 2026 markets list includes active developments in Chicago Hoffman Estates, Northern Virginia Loudoun County, Toronto, and Milan, plus a newly broken-ground site in Meridian, Mississippi, alongside earlier markets including Minneapolis and Nashville that the company has since exited or transferred to independent ownership. Separately, Compass donated 12.6 million dollars to fund a 40,000 square foot workforce-training replica data center at 300 Houston School Road in Red Oak, operated by Texas State Technical College, a distinct facility from the wholesale buildings mapped here that should not be confused with them. No per-building capacity, square footage, tenant, or year-built figure could be confirmed for this specific structure, and no local government permit or tax-abatement record could be retrieved this session, so those figures are deliberately omitted rather than estimated from campus-wide totals.

reading.body:
Compass Red Oak Campus is Compass Datacenters' flagship Texas hyperscale site, located south of Dallas on approximately 800 to 830 acres as of a May 2026 expansion approval. The operator has announced a full build-out target of over 350 MW of IT load from a January 2020 groundbreaking, but no current confirmed operating capacity figure is published, so the campus does not appear in the 468 MW of published IT capacity tracked across Texas. Trade press from 2024 to 2026 describes multiple completed phases and construction underway, including at least one one-million-square-foot building already operational and named subprojects targeting 2025 to 2026 completion.

The site's complexity makes precise ranking difficult. The registry maps 11 Compass Data Center rows in the Ellis County area, all sharing a generic name with no distinguishing building labels in the source data, and two different building-naming conventions appear in trade press and aggregator sourcing with direct address conflicts between them. No individual row in this registry can be reliably mapped to a specific named building, phase, or street address without guessing. As a result, no specific address or building identity is assigned to this row, leaving an honest gap rather than an uncertain claim.

The campus sits in a state where 18 of 133 mapped data center facilities publish capacity figures. Compass has framed expansion as a long-term community commitment, establishing a technician training partnership with Texas State Technical College and proposing a 15 million dollar grant for a municipal animal shelter in Red Oak in response to local opposition to recent expansion. The binding constraint on whether this campus matters to AI scaling remains unknown: neither current operating power draw nor grid interconnection capacity is published.
